briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: From Zalympix Gold to Schedule III Holding Firm: Momentum Builds for Operators
briefs.top: Michigan cannabis had plenty to celebrate this week — Zalympix gold medals, a $17B sales milestone, and a gubernatorial candidate now courting the industry against the 24% wholesale tax — even as distressed real estate opens the door for well-capitalized buyers. Nationally, rescheduling survived another court challenge and Compass Pathways landed a fast-tracked FDA review for its psilocybin therapy, adding fresh tailwinds industry-wide.

local.text: Michigan cultivators sweep the 'Grammys of Cannabis' — Mitten Canna Co.'s Toad Venom and Hytek's Oishii Piña took the top flower and rosin prizes at this year's Zalympix, with winners crowned Saturday night at the Crofoot in Pontiac in front of 27 flower finalists and 20 rosin finalists from across Michigan.

GOP governor hopeful courts industry on tax repeal — John James, the Republican candidate for governor, has taken a position against the wholesale tax, saying he'd support repeal or a sharp reduction, earning the endorsement of the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association.

State cannabis sales cross $17 billion since 2019 — Michigan has surpassed $17 billion in combined adult-use and medical marijuana sales since regulated sales began, with August alone generating roughly $259.09 million.

Distressed real estate opens door for savvy buyers — at least 50 cannabis properties are now up for sale or lease across the state, with one broker saying they're selling for 20 to 30 cents on the dollar.

Industry presses fresh legal challenge to wholesale tax — Michigan's marijuana industry has filed a second lawsuit challenging the wholesale tax, arguing it effectively sets a higher rate than the 6% sales tax cap in the state constitution.

national.text: Rescheduling survives another court challenge — reclassification opponents filed a lawsuit to stop medical marijuana's change in schedule, but that challenge was rebuffed this week in federal court.

Compass Pathways scores FDA fast-track review — the FDA granted Compass a rolling NDA review and awarded COMP360 a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for treatment-resistant depression, built on positive Phase 3 data.
Trump commutes federal marijuana sentences — President Trump commutes 30-year and 10-year federal marijuana sentences, extending executive-level relief for legacy cannabis offenders.

Hemp THC ban pushed back again — Trump signed a short-term funding bill pushing back scheduled federal restrictions on hemp-derived THC products from November 12 to December 11, 2026, buying operators more runway.

State cannabis tax hauls keep climbing — state governments reported $986.8 million in marijuana tax collections in Q2 2026, up about 11% year-over-year and nearly 16% versus Q1, pushing 2026 collections to roughly $1.84 billion.
